literal: Than good association, greater companion there is not; than evil association, suffering that which causes also there is not.
translation: There is no companion greater than good association, and there is nothing that brings more suffering than evil association.
modern: நல்ல சேர்க்கையை விடச் சிறந்த துணை வேறு இல்லை; தீய சேர்க்கையை விடத் துன்பத்தைத் தருவது வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet highlights the powerful influence of the company we keep. The poet uses a parallel structure to contrast good and bad associations. Good company is described as the ultimate support system, with no helper or companion ('துணை') exceeding it. Conversely, bad company is identified as the ultimate source of misery, with nothing else causing as much deep suffering ('அல்லல்'). The word 'படுப்பதூஉம்' uses a poetic elongation to emphasize the inevitable and heavy toll that bad associations inflict on a person.
